edition.en: Gitanjali (London, 1912), Tagore’s own English prose translations, from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; poems 1, 5, 7, 11, 13, 60, 63, 69, 82 and 103, with their original numbers
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《吉檀迦利》（伦敦，1912），泰戈尔自译的英文散文诗；选第 1、5、7、11、13、60、63、69、82、103 首，保留原编号

basis.en: Published in 1912 in the author’s own English translation; the author died in 1941.
basis.zh: 1912 年出版，英文为作者自译；作者卒于 1941 年。

note.en: Ten of the 103 prose poems in Gitanjali, which Tagore translated into English himself from his Bengali songs and published in London in 1912; the next year he received the Nobel Prize in Literature. Notice how often they are about unfinished things: a song not yet sung, a lamp not yet lit, and the patience of a “thou” who “knowest how to wait”.
note.zh: 《吉檀迦利》一百零三首散文诗中的十首。泰戈尔亲自把自己的孟加拉语歌诗译成英文，1912 年在伦敦出版；第二年他获得诺贝尔文学奖。留意这些诗多么常写未完成的事：一首还没唱出的歌、一盏还没点亮的灯，以及那位“懂得等待”的“你”的耐心。

excerpt.orig: Thy centuries follow each other perfecting a small wild flower.
excerpt.en: Thy centuries follow each other perfecting a small wild flower.
excerpt.zh: 你的世纪一个接着一个，只为使一朵小小的野花臻于完美。

note.en: Tagore’s own English versions, which won him the Nobel Prize, are luminous in places, but their archaic diction loses much of the Bengali songs’ music.
note.zh: 泰戈尔自译的英文本，为他赢得诺贝尔奖；不少段落澄澈，但古旧的措辞失去了孟加拉语原歌的音乐。
